literal: For those who destroyed any virtue, escape there will be; escape there is not for the man who destroyed a benefit done.
translation: There may be salvation for those who have destroyed any other virtue; but there is no salvation for the person who has destroyed gratitude by forgetting a benefit done.
modern: எந்த அறத்தை அழித்தவர்க்கும் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க வழி உண்டு; ஆனால், ஒருவர் செய்த உதவியை மறந்து அழித்த மனிதனுக்குத் தப்பிப் பிழைக்க வழியே இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme gravity of ingratitude. The author states that even for those who commit the worst sins or destroy other great virtues, there is still a way to redeem themselves or escape ruin. However, for the person who destroys a benefit done to them, there is absolutely no way of escape or redemption. The word 'கொன்ற' (literally 'killed' or 'destroyed') is used powerfully here to mean utterly wiping out or forgetting a good deed, showing that ingratitude is viewed as a fatal moral crime.
